newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht falls to new record low on peso jitters.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht falls to new record low on peso jitters.

text.p: The Thai baht fell to a new record low of 29.750 to the dollar early on Friday in line with the battered Philippine peso and heavy local demand for the greenback, dealers said.
"It has definitely been hurt by the Philippine peso attacks. Speculators are focusing on both the Philippine and Thai currencies," a dealer at a Thai bank said.
The baht retreated sharply at the opening from 29.100/29.200 late on Thursday.
Another local dealer said the baht was hit by current weak market sentiment on most South East Asian currencies. "We saw some bids for dollar at around 30.000 baht this morning," he said.
Another dealer in Singapore said: "The whole region has been affected by the Philippine peso. I would not call it panic baht selling."
Dealers said, however, that baht/dollar trade was partly restrained by a sustained Thai central bank policy to block access of offshore baht for foreign speculators.
A Thai dealer said the baht weakness could also be attributed to high carried over commercial demand for dollars that was unmatched at the Thursday close.
"Some unmatched bids for dollar on Thursday needed to be squared this morning," he said.
Dealers said they still had not detected any signs that the Thai central bank had stepped in to defend the baht.
The Bank of Thailand announced a de facto devaluation of the baht on July 2 by letting it loose in a new managed float regime.
The Thai overnight interbank rate rose to 20-22 percent this morning from 15-20 late on Thursday on strong demand for baht funds to buy dollar, dealers said.
"Heavy dollar buying would keep interbank rates high today. But I don't think the rates will shoot up as they are already exceptionally high," said a money market dealer at a foreign bank.
